title: Sulphur monoxide emission tracing an embedded planet in the HD 100546 protoplanetary disk
question: What is the spatial morphology, kinematics, and chemical/physical origin of the sulphur monoxide (SO) emission in the HD 100546 protoplanetary disk, and is it connected to embedded forming giant planets?

recipe.goal: Calibrate, combine, and image continuum and molecular lines (SO, SiO, SiS)
recipe.method: Combine self-calibrated short-baseline (43C-2) data with pipeline-calibrated long-baseline (43C-5) data, perform phase and amplitude self-calibration, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, concatenate the two SO spectral windows using concat, image continuum and lines across a Briggs robust grid (+1.0, +0.5, 0.0, -0.5) using tCLEAN with multi-scale deconvolver and Keplerian masking, and apply the JvM correction.
key_parameters: Velocity binning: 0.12 km s^-1 for SO, 0.25 km s^-1 (or 0.24 km s^-1) for SiO and SiS
JvM epsilon ~ 0.50 for robust +0.5 line images (0.56 for robust 0.5 continuum)

recipe.goal: Extract disk-integrated spectra, measure integrated line fluxes/upper limits, and constrain inner emitting radius from kinematics
recipe.method: Extract spectra from an elliptical aperture of semi-major axis 0.6'' matching the disk inclination and PA; integrate SO line profiles between +/-7.5 km s^-1 around the source velocity; compute 3-sigma upper limits for SiO and SiS; determine the inner ring radius of SO from the maximum velocity drop-off assuming Keplerian rotation.
assumptions: Keplerian rotation around a stellar dynamical mass of 2.2 M_sun, source velocity of 5.7 km s^-1, and disk inclination angle of 32 deg (or 40 deg)

recipe.goal: Extract radial emission profiles via spectral shifting and stacking
recipe.method: Shift and stack spectra from each pixel in the channel maps within concentric annuli of width 0.05'' using GoFish, calculating errors per radial bin from the rms in the shifted spectra.

recipe.goal: Derive radial, azimuthal, and disk-averaged column densities and abundance ratios
recipe.method: Convert radial emission profiles, azimuthal integrated intensity profiles at r = 20 au, and 0.6'' integrated fluxes/upper limits into column densities of SO, SiO, and SiS assuming optically thin LTE emission at fixed rotational temperatures, averaging the two detected SO transitions.
key_parameters: Inner disk emitting area = 1.8 x 10^-11 steradians (0.6'' ellipse)
assumptions: Optically thin emission and local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE)
Rotational temperature T_rot = 75, 100, 200 K for inner disk (<100 au) and 30, 40, 50 K for outer disk (>100 au)

score_reason: Observing setup, spectral windows, software versions (CASA 5.6.0, GoFish, keplerian_mask), Briggs robust values, JvM epsilon factors, velocity integration ranges, and LTE column density assumptions are all clearly documented. However, exact self-calibration solution intervals, tCLEAN cell/image sizes and stopping thresholds, and Keplerian mask parameters are inherited from external papers or omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data (2019.1.00193.S) with clear quantitative targets: integrated line fluxes, inner cavity radius from kinematics, factor-of-2 azimuthal asymmetry, GoFish radial profile showing the second ring at ~200 au, and LTE column densities.
